learningObjective: Understand CUDA stream and event semantics: intra-stream ordering, inter-stream overlap, event-based sync.

canonicalClaims.claim: Within one non-default CUDA stream, work is serialized in issue order; different streams may execute concurrently subject to hardware resources. Events (`cudaEventRecord` on one stream + `cudaStreamWaitEvent` on another) provide asynchronous cross-stream ordering without blocking the host.
nonImplications: Does not imply any two streams always run in parallel.
Does not imply events block the host.

misconceptions.claim: Non-default streams block each other by default.
misconceptions.whyWrong: They are concurrent by default; overlap subject to resources.

misconceptions.claim: `cudaEventRecord` blocks the CPU until the device processes it.
misconceptions.whyWrong: It is asynchronous; use `cudaEventSynchronize` to block the host.
It adds a wait to the specified stream on the device side; host is not blocked.

misconceptions.claim: The default stream (0) behaves identically to any other stream.
misconceptions.whyWrong: Legacy default stream synchronizes with all others; per-thread default stream is another mode; behavior is compile-flag dependent.

implementationFacts: Compile flag `--default-stream per-thread` changes default-stream semantics.
